name: find
description: Searches for files and directories in a directory hierarchy, matching by name, size, time, type, permissions, and more, and can execute actions on results.

flags.description: Match file names, case-sensitively; -iname ignores case. Wildcards must be quoted.
Match files larger than 100 megabytes (units: c, k, M, G).
Modified within the last 7 days; +7 means older than 7 days.
-perm MODE: match by owner / permission bits.
Run CMD on each match, replacing {} with the path. Use \+ to batch.
Descend at most N directory levels.
Delete matched files (use with extreme care).

examples.explanation: Finds all .log files under the current directory, at any depth. Quotes prevent the shell from expanding the pattern first.
Finds rotated logs older than 30 days — typical candidates for cleanup.
Lists every file over 100 MB with human-readable sizes.
Searches for .js files while skipping node_modules trees (-prune stops descending into them).
Shows files modified in the last 24 hours.
Deletes all .tmp files under the current tree. Always run the same find without -delete first to preview.

about: find walks the directory tree and evaluates an expression for each entry. Expressions combine tests (-name, -type, -size), operators (-and, -or, !), and actions (-print, -exec, -delete). If no action is given, -print is implied.
GNU find adds -printf for custom output formats, -regextype for different regex flavors, and -quit to stop after the first match.
useCases: Locate files by name, size, age, or owner.
Bulk operations: change permissions, delete, or compress matched files.
Clean up build artifacts and old logs.
mistakes: Forgetting quotes around -name patterns, letting the shell expand them first.
Using -exec {} \; in a loop when {} \+ or xargs would be far faster.
Running -delete before previewing the match list.
warnings: find -delete acts immediately and irreversibly. Build the expression, verify the output, then add -delete as the last action.
distroNotes: GNU find (findutils) supports -printf, -regextype, and -quit. BSD find lacks -printf and uses different regex defaults.
